messages.subject: Factor Scores in Lavaan
parts:
Dear Lavaan Team,

I am Priyanka Pereira, a PhD candidate at the University of Twente in The Netherlands. I have just used Lavaan to conduct a confirmatory factor analysis. Everything went well. Thank you very much for this easy-to-use package!

I would now like to use the factor scores to do the following:

  • Find the mean and standard deviation for each factor
  • Evaluate the prediction of a certain factor by a few of the other factors
  • Investigate the (possible) latent classes among the respondents 

I have used the lavPredict function to obtain the factor scores. However, when I calculate the correlations between these factor scores, they do not match the correlations obtained from the summary of the model.

Therefore, I have a few questions:

  1. Can the lavPredict function handle ordinal data?
  2. Are the correlations calculated using the factor scores? If yes, how are these factor scores calculated?
  3. I understand that the factor scores from the lavPredict function are calculated as the sum of each item multiplied by its respective factor score weight: Sum (Item1Score x Item1FactorScoreWeight + Item2Score x Item2FactorScoreWeight + …). Is this understanding correct?
  4. If the answer to question 2 is yes, is it acceptable for me to have one set of factor scores (from the summary of the model) for the correlations between the factors, and another set of factor scores (from the lavPredict function) for the three points listed above?
  5. Unfortunately, the factor scores obtained via the lavPredict function are like z scores. How can I use these to continue with the three points listed above? For example, the mean of each factor turns out to be (close to) 0.

Thank you very much for your time and guidance!

Kind regards,

Priyanka Pereira

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Factor Scores in Lavaan
parts:
Priyanka--
     If you want factor means and variances, there are model parameter estimates that provide those. The "factor scores" that lavaan provides do not actually match the factors themselves. Actual factor scores must include an additional arbitrary component due to the phenomenon of factor indeterminacy. Basically, the factors are underdetermined by the data. See, for example, Grice (2001):
Grice, J. W. (2001). Computing and evaluating factor scores. Psychological methods, 6(4), 430.
     This documentation page answers your question about ordinal data:
https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/lavaan/html/lavPredict.html
     The means and variances of common factors are arbitrary--the factors are statistical fabrications with no actual existence, so their moments only have values relative to something else. If you don't want the means to be 0, add something to them. In a multiple group model, means in some groups will be relative to means in other groups. Variances are similarly arbitrary.
--Ed Rigdon
